plugin_desc: SNMP monitoring template for Arista switch. It reports uptime, CPU utilization, memory utilization, temperature, fan, power supply status, optical modules, and interface traffic, for EOS data-center switches (based on standard MIBs).
name: Switch

metrics.name: device_cpu_usage
metrics.description: CPU utilization of the Arista EOS switch (HOST-RESOURCES hrProcessorLoad, averaged across cores). Sustained high CPU may indicate control-plane or routing-process load.

metrics.name: device_memory_used
metrics.description: This metric reports the number of bytes currently in use by Arista EOS system RAM (HOST-RESOURCES hrStorageUsed on the RAM row selected by hrStorageDescr, multiplied by hrStorageAllocationUnits). It helps administrators understand absolute memory consumption and identify when the device is under memory pressure.

metrics.name: device_memory_total
metrics.description: This metric reports the total size in bytes of Arista EOS system RAM (HOST-RESOURCES hrStorageSize on the RAM row selected by hrStorageDescr, multiplied by hrStorageAllocationUnits). Together with the used bytes it determines overall memory utilization.

metrics.name: device_memory_usage
metrics.description: This metric reports overall memory utilization of the Arista EOS switch, computed as used / total * 100 from HOST-RESOURCES RAM rows. High memory usage may indicate memory leaks, oversized routing/MAC/ARP tables, or insufficient capacity, and can cause instability or failed allocations.

metrics.name: device_temperature_celsius
metrics.description: This metric reports the highest chassis ENTITY-SENSOR temperature reading on the Arista EOS switch, in degrees Celsius. Only sensors whose type is celsius and whose descr is not a DOM module sensor are kept, and the raw value is converted with entPhySensorScale and entPhySensorPrecision. Abnormally high temperatures may indicate fan failure, blocked airflow, or excessive ambient heat.

metrics.name: device_fan_state
metrics.description: This metric reports the operational state of each Arista EOS cooling fan (ENTITY-STATE-MIB entStateOper joined with ENTITY-MIB entPhysicalClass fan=7), normalized so that 1 means ok (enabled) and 2 means bad. A non-ok state indicates a cooling fault that can quickly lead to overheating and should be investigated immediately.

metrics.name: device_psu_state
metrics.description: This metric reports the operational state of each Arista EOS power supply (ENTITY-STATE-MIB entStateOper joined with ENTITY-MIB entPhysicalClass powerSupply=6), normalized so that 1 means ok (enabled) and 2 means bad. A non-ok state signals a power redundancy or hardware fault and must be remediated promptly.

metrics.name: device_optical_rx_power
metrics.description: Per-sensor optical receive power in dBm from ENTITY-SENSOR-MIB entPhySensorTable. Rows are selected when entPhysicalDescr or entPhysicalName contains DOM RX Power (case-insensitive). The raw value is converted with entPhySensorScale and entPhySensorPrecision. A dropping RX level is an early sign of fiber attenuation, dirty optics, or a failing peer transmitter.

metrics.name: device_optical_tx_power
metrics.description: Per-sensor optical transmit power in dBm from ENTITY-SENSOR-MIB entPhySensorTable. Rows are selected when entPhysicalDescr or entPhysicalName contains DOM TX Power (case-insensitive). The raw value is converted with entPhySensorScale and entPhySensorPrecision. An abnormally low TX level indicates a failing laser/optic rather than fiber attenuation alone.

metrics.name: device_optical_temperature
metrics.description: Per-sensor optical-module temperature in degrees Celsius from ENTITY-SENSOR-MIB. Rows are selected when sensor type is celsius and descr contains DOM. The raw value is converted with entPhySensorScale and entPhySensorPrecision. Abnormally high module temperature can precede laser degradation or link errors.

metrics.name: interface_ifHCInOctets
metrics.description: This metric indicates the average rate of bytes received over the past 5 minutes, measured in bytes per second, from the 64-bit IF-MIB ifHCInOctets counter (ifXTable). The 64-bit counter avoids the rapid wrap of the 32-bit ifInOctets on high-speed switch ports, keeping the rate accurate.

metrics.name: interface_ifHCOutOctets
metrics.description: This metric calculates the average rate of bytes sent over the past 5 minutes, measured in bytes per second, from the 64-bit IF-MIB ifHCOutOctets counter (ifXTable). The 64-bit counter avoids the rapid wrap of the 32-bit ifOutOctets on high-speed switch ports, keeping the rate accurate.

metrics.name: snmp_uptime
metrics.description: This metric indicates the uptime of the device since the last restart. By monitoring the uptime, network administrators can understand the stability and reliability of the device and identify potential reboot or failure issues.
